site.name: Zagros
site.meta_description: Sudan's trusted partner for agricultural inputs since 2010. Seeds from Thailand and Australia, fertilizers from Germany and the Netherlands, pesticides from Egypt, Switzerland, the UK, India, and China.

about.title: About
about.headline: Sudan's full-input agricultural-solutions partner since 2010.
about.deck: Zagros Trading has served Sudanese farms — from ministry-scale projects to family operations — for sixteen years. Six branches, seven international suppliers, three product lines under one roof. Consultancy, distribution, and after-sales support.
about.pillar_1_body: Agronomy desk on every order over a soil report's worth of complexity. Composition-first, not catalog-first.
about.pillar_2_body: Salt-stress, high-pH, low-rainfall, hot summers — the catalog is curated for what Sudanese fields actually face.
about.pillar_3_body: Seven international suppliers across six countries. K+S German chemistry, Barenbrug Australian breeding, East West Thai vegetable hybrids. EU Organic certifications where the brief calls for them.

editors_note.headline: What separates an input distributor from a soil partner
editors_note.para1_body: he difference shows up at the second cut, not the bag. Anyone can move a pallet — fewer can tell you which K source won't lock out the calcium you'll need at fruit set, or why the irrigated lucerne block needs a different rate sheet than the rainfed one next door.
editors_note.para2: Issue 03 is built around three trials our agronomy desk audited in the last quarter — salt-stress tomato, citrus magnesium, and a side-by-side lucerne yield read. Each one is here because a customer asked us the question first.
editors_note.pull_quote: Specs forward. Data first. The bag arrives last.
editors_note.para3: If the catalog reads more like a service manual than a brochure, that's on purpose. Yield is the metric. Everything else is footnotes.
